artifacts.summary: Research for both folded parts: (1) replacing the static BUILD_HEAVY_TASK_TYPES family list with a measured wall-clock signal already captured in metrics.jsonl, plus explicit no-history fallback options, with job-count ruled out as a previously-declined path; (2) transcription-ready evidence for appending the repo-scanning-pollution and mode-2 bare-invocation-bypass hazard classes plus the CoW/reflink/overlayfs/clone-nothing evaluation to batch-orchestration-guardrails.md's isolation posture section, sourced from task 301's archived report and the reaffirmation decision record.

memory_candidates.content: specs/{NNN}_{SLUG}/metrics.jsonl (written by dispatch-metrics.sh) already records per-dispatch wall_clock_seconds keyed by task directory and phase (including 'implement'), with zero gaps for a task that has had at least one prior implement dispatch. Any future admission/scheduling heuristic needing a measured per-task build-duration signal should read this file via the existing task_lookup_dir() idiom rather than inventing new capture instrumentation.

lake-build-guard.sh deliberately does NOT parse Lake's build output for a job count, to avoid coupling the guard to Lake's output format (documented in its own header as 'the plan's Decision 3'); Lake 5.0.0 also exposes no -j/--jobs flag. Any future design wanting a job-count-based signal for Lean/Lake builds is re-opening an already-declined path, not filling a gap.
